name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
description: Regeneron invents antibody medicines and sells some itself and partners on others. Its own sales are the eye drug EYLEA and its higher-dose successor EYLEA HD (sold in the US by Regeneron, outside the US by Bayer) and Libtayo for skin and other cancers. The bigger profit engine is now collaboration revenue: Sanofi pays Regeneron its share of Dupixent profits, which was 41 percent of total 2025 revenue, and Bayer pays its share of ex-US EYLEA sales. Regeneron reports one segment and has paid a quarterly dividend since 2025.

gics.note: Conventional GICS sector and sub-industry per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30); that list does not show the industry group or industry, so those are null.

hq.note: 777 Old Saw Mill River Road, Tarrytown, NY 10591 (EDGAR business address)

businessLines.name: Net product sales (Regeneron sells directly)
businessLines.how: Sells injected medicines (eye injections given in retina clinics, cancer infusions) through specialty distributors, at list price less rebates. Concentrated: EYLEA HD plus EYLEA in the US were 31% of total revenue in 2025 (42% in 2024).

businessLines.name: Sanofi collaboration revenue (mostly Dupixent profit share)
businessLines.how: Regeneron invented Dupixent with Sanofi; Sanofi sells it and Regeneron books its share of the profits as collaboration revenue (the 10-K says most of this line is the Dupixent profit share). No manufacturing or selling cost on Regeneron's side for this stream beyond the collaboration terms; terms not extracted.

businessLines.name: Bayer collaboration revenue (ex-US EYLEA / EYLEA HD)
businessLines.how: Bayer sells EYLEA outside the US; Regeneron receives its share as collaboration revenue (terms not extracted).

businessLines.name: Other collaboration and other revenue
businessLines.how: Other partner payments and miscellaneous income (not itemised in the excerpt read).
